builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
summary: SteerDistill replaces standard post-training quantization (PTQ) or quantized LoRA methods that treat behavioral drift as a static weight-approximation problem. It requires a full-precision teacher model and an iterative training loop where the teacher steers the student through rollouts to correct environment-specific failures, adding significant complexity to the training pipeline. Adoption may fail if the full-precision teacher cannot accurately guide the student in specific environmental contexts or if the student lacks the capacity to internalize steered behaviors without guidance.
rationale: While the method improves the reliability of 4-bit agents, it requires a full-precision teacher and a multi-stage iterative training loop that exceeds the 'no foundation-model training' and limited infrastructure constraints of a single 24 GB GPU environment.
technique: Closed-loop teacher steering for quantized agents

claims.statement: SteerDistill replaces standard post-training quantization (PTQ) or quantized LoRA methods that treat behavioral drift as a static weight-approximation problem. It requires a full-precision teacher model and an iterative training loop where the teacher steers the student through rollouts to correct environment-specific failures, adding significant complexity to the training pipeline. Adoption may fail if the full-precision teacher cannot accurately guide the student in specific environmental contexts or if the student lacks the capacity to internalize steered behaviors without guidance.

Exceeds the strongest quantized baseline by 1.67-2.18 points in average score under W4A16 and stays within one point of BF16. On τ²-Bench, outperforms QeRL by 1.84 percentage points in success rate using 67% fewer training GPU hours.
